prompt: What is the definition of an obligation under Article 1156 of the New Civil Code of the Philippines?

choices.text: Juridical necessity to do or not to do.
Juridical necessity to give or not to give.
Juridical necessity to give, to do or not to do.
Juridical necessity to give, not to give, to do or not to do.

rationale: Article 1156 NCC defines obligation as a juridical necessity to give, to do or not to do.
canonicalConcept: Definition of obligation under Article 1156 NCC

prompt: The following are the essential elements of an obligation, except

choices.text: An active subject, who has the power to demand prestation, also known as the obligee or creditor.
Object or prestation, which is the promise or particular conduct to be performed.
Efficient cause, the tie which binds the parties to the obligation, also known as juridical tie or vinculum.
The form in which the obligation is entered into.

rationale: The essential elements are active subject, passive subject, object/prestation, and efficient cause. Form is not essential unless required by law.
canonicalConcept: Essential elements of an obligation

prompt: The following are the sources of civil obligation demandable in a court of law, except

choices.text: Quasi-delicts or Culpa Aquiliana or Torts

rationale: Under Article 1157 NCC, sources are law, contracts, quasi-contracts, delicts, and quasi-delicts. Religious doctrines are not a source of civil obligations.
canonicalConcept: Sources of civil obligations under Article 1157 NCC

prompt: What is the source of obligation of parents to provide support to their children?
rationale: The obligation of parents to support children is imposed by law (Family Code), not by contract.
canonicalConcept: Source of parental support obligation

prompt: Negligence or culpa which results to civil liability arising from quasi-delict or torts is also known as
rationale: Culpa aquiliana is negligence resulting in civil liability from quasi-delict under Article 2176 NCC.
canonicalConcept: Classification of culpa: culpa aquiliana vs culpa contractual vs culpa criminal

prompt: In an obligation to deliver a determinate thing, what degree of diligence shall be exercised by the obligor or debtor in the preservation of the determinate or specific or delimited generic thing?

choices.text: Extraordinary diligence unless the law or stipulation requires another standard.
Diligence of a father of a good family unless the law or stipulation requires another standard.
Diligence of a good father of a family or ordinary diligence unless the law or stipulation requires another standard.
No diligence unless the law or stipulation requires another standard.

rationale: Article 1163 NCC requires diligence of a good father of a family (ordinary diligence) in preserving the specific thing.
canonicalConcept: Degree of diligence required for obligations to deliver determinate things

prompt: What is the status of a contract entered into during a lucid interval?
rationale: Article 1328 NCC: contracts entered into during a lucid interval are valid.
canonicalConcept: Capacity to contract: contracts during lucid intervals of insane persons

prompt: The following are the requisites of an offer, except
rationale: An offer must be definite, complete, and intentional. Uncertainty makes it vague and incapable of acceptance.
canonicalConcept: Requisites of a valid offer in contract formation

prompt: An audit staff and an auditing firm orally entered into a contract of employment whereby it is stipulated that overtime premium and holiday pay are waived. Is the waiver valid?

choices.text: Yes because of mutuality of contract.
Yes because of autonomy of contract.
No because it is contrary to law and public policy.
No because it is entered into orally but not in writing.

rationale: Waiver of overtime premium and holiday pay is contrary to mandatory provisions of the Labor Code and public policy.
canonicalConcept: Defective contracts: stipulations contrary to law and public policy

prompt: Consensual contracts are perfected by

choices.text: Delivery of the object of a contract.
Execution of formalities required by law.
Provisions of the New Civil Code.

rationale: Consensual contracts like sale are perfected by mere consent. Real contracts require delivery; formal contracts require formalities.
canonicalConcept: Perfection of consensual contracts vs real contracts vs formal contracts

prompt: If mistake, fraud, inequitable conduct or accident has prevented a meeting of the minds of the parties, what is the proper remedy?

choices.text: Ask for reformation of the instrument.
Ask for annulment of the contract.
Ask for rescission of the contract.

rationale: When there is no meeting of the minds, the contract is voidable and the remedy is annulment. Reformation applies when there is a meeting of minds but the instrument does not reflect it.
canonicalConcept: Remedy when no meeting of the minds exists: annulment vs reformation

prompt: It is a contract that has caused a particular damage to one of the parties or to a third person, and which for equitable reasons may be set aside even if it is valid.
rationale: Rescissible contracts are valid but cause economic damage and may be set aside for equitable reasons (Article 1381 NCC).
canonicalConcept: Rescissible contracts: definition and characteristics

prompt: The following are void contracts except:

choices.text: Analyn who sold Richard a parcel of land in the Moon.
X hired Y to kill Vice President A in exchange of Php 1 Million.
Jonas hired Karl to build a time machine in six months time.
Arjay and Jeremy both minors entered into a contract of sale of a Toyota Vios.

rationale: Contracts by minors are voidable, not void. Impossible objects (moon land, time machine) and illegal objects (assassination) make contracts void.
canonicalConcept: Void vs voidable contracts: contracts with minors are voidable not void

prompt: The following may ask for the reformation of an instrument, except

choices.text: Either party if the mistake is mutual.
Successors in interest, heirs and assigns of injured party.

rationale: The guilty party cannot ask for reformation. Only the injured party, either party in mutual mistake, and successors in interest may seek reformation.
canonicalConcept: Parties entitled to reformation of instruments

prompt: To defraud his creditors, Miguel sold his real property to Liza. Liza now seeks to register the sale. Lester, a creditor seeks to prevent the registration on the ground that it is a rescissible contract. Is Lester's statement correct?

choices.text: No, because the contract is not rescissible.
No, because the sale is void.
Yes, because it is a rescissible contract as it was taken in fraud of creditors.

rationale: Article 1381 NCC: contracts entered into in fraud of creditors are rescissible. The creditor may seek rescission to satisfy his claim.
canonicalConcept: Rescissible contracts in fraud of creditors under Article 1381 NCC

prompt: The following are the requisites of consent, except
rationale: The requisites of consent are that it must be intelligent, free, and spontaneous (or manifest). 'Manifest' is the standard third requisite.
canonicalConcept: Requisites of consent in contracts

prompt: Who among the following persons is capacitated to give consent to a contract?

choices.text: Minor or Person below 18 years of age.
Deaf mute who do not know how to read and write.

rationale: An insane person during a lucid interval has capacity to contract. Minors, demented persons, and deaf-mutes who cannot read/write lack capacity.
canonicalConcept: Contractual capacity: lucid intervals of insane persons

prompt: What is the name of the contract if the goods are to be manufactured especially for the customer upon his special order and not for the general market?

choices.text: Contract for a piece of work.

rationale: When goods are manufactured specially for a customer upon special order, it is a contract for a piece of work (locatio conductio operis), not a contract of sale.
canonicalConcept: Contract for a piece of work vs contract of sale

prompt: What is the effect of gross inadequacy of price in a contract of sale?

choices.text: It renders the contract of sale null and void.
It renders the contract of sale unenforceable.

It does not affect a contract of sale, except as it may indicate a defect in the consent which makes the contract voidable or except as it may indicate that the intention of the parties is another contract such as donation or loan with equitable mortgage.
It does not affect a contract of sale even if the parties really intended a donation or some other act or contract.

rationale: Article 1355 NCC: gross inadequacy of price does not affect validity unless it indicates vitiation of consent or a different contract was intended.
canonicalConcept: Effect of gross inadequacy of price in sales under Article 1355 NCC

prompt: S and B entered into a contract of sale of a specific car. S delivered the key of the car to B. What type of constructive delivery is present?
rationale: Traditio symbolica (traditio clavium) is delivery by means of symbols, such as delivering the key to a car.
canonicalConcept: Modes of delivery in sales: traditio symbolica/clavium

prompt: It is a stipulation whereby the thing pledged or mortgaged shall automatically become the property of the creditor in the event of non-payment of the debt within the term fixed.
rationale: Pactum commissorium is the prohibited stipulation that the pledged/mortgaged property shall automatically become the creditor's property upon default.
canonicalConcept: Pactum commissorium in pledge and mortgage

prompt: What is the nature of a contract of pledge?
rationale: A contract of pledge is a real contract perfected by delivery of the thing pledged.
canonicalConcept: Nature of pledge as a real contract

prompt: The following may become object of chattel mortgage, except
rationale: Chattel mortgage covers only personal/movable property. Real property is subject to real estate mortgage.
canonicalConcept: Object of chattel mortgage: personal/movable property only

prompt: Frank borrowed P1,000,000 from his brother Eric. To pay the loan, Frank issued a post-dated check to be presented for payment a month after the transaction. Two days before maturity, Frank called Eric telling him he had insufficient funds and requested that the deposit of the check be deferred. Nevertheless, Eric deposited the check and it was dishonored. When Frank failed to pay despite demand, Eric filed a complaint against him for violation of Batas Pambansa Blg. 22. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: Good faith is a defense for violation of BP 22.
The request of Frank to defer the deposit of the check as it has insufficient funds will militate against his prosecution for BP 22.

rationale: Good faith is not a defense in BP 22. The mere issuance of a check knowing it would be dishonored is sufficient. Frank's request to defer does not absolve him.
canonicalConcept: BP 22 violation: good faith is not a defense

prompt: A asked financial support from her showbiz friend B who accommodated her by issuing in her favor a postdated check in the sum of P90,000.00. Both of them knew that the check would not be honored because B's account had just been closed. The two then approached trader C whom they asked to change the check with cash, even agreeing that the exchange be discounted at P85,000.00 with the assurance that the check shall be funded upon maturity. Upon C's presentment of the check for payment on due date, it was dishonored because the account had already been closed. What crime is committed in the above case?
rationale: The facts constitute a violation of BP 22. Both A and B knew the check was worthless when issued. While estafa may also be committed, BP 22 is the direct answer based on the specific facts.
canonicalConcept: BP 22 vs Estafa: issuance of check with closed account

prompt: Which of the following motor vehicles is protected by the Lemon Law rights period?

choices.text: Brand new motor vehicle purchased in the Philippines.
Second-hand motor vehicle purchased in the Philippines.

rationale: The Lemon Law (RA 10642) applies to brand new motor vehicles purchased in the Philippines. It does not cover second-hand vehicles.
canonicalConcept: Lemon Law coverage: brand new motor vehicles only

prompt: They are considered goods vital to the needs of consumers for their sustenance and existence during the times enumerated in the Price Act.
rationale: Basic necessities are goods vital to consumers for sustenance and existence, such as rice, corn, bread, meat, etc.
canonicalConcept: Basic necessities under the Price Act

prompt: What legal remedy is available to an individual debtor who, possessing sufficient property to cover all his debts but foreseeing the impossibility of meeting them when they respectively fall due, may desire to ask the court for relief?

choices.text: Petition for declaration of state of suspension of payments.

rationale: Suspension of payments is for a debtor with sufficient property but foresees inability to pay when debts fall due. Rehabilitation is for insolvent debtors.
canonicalConcept: Suspension of payments vs rehabilitation vs liquidation

prompt: It shall refer to the order issued by the court evidencing the commencement of the rehabilitation proceedings.
rationale: The Commencement Order is issued by the court to signify the start of rehabilitation proceedings.
canonicalConcept: Commencement order in rehabilitation proceedings

prompt: It is a type of court-supervised rehabilitation wherein it is the insolvent businessman who filed the petition for rehabilitation before the rehabilitation court.
rationale: Voluntary court-supervised rehabilitation is initiated by the debtor himself. Involuntary is filed by creditors.
canonicalConcept: Voluntary vs involuntary court-supervised rehabilitation

prompt: It refers to the power of the rehabilitation court to approve and implement a rehabilitation plan notwithstanding the objection of the majority of creditors. It forces the creditors to accept the terms and conditions of the rehabilitation plan, preferring long-term viability over immediate but incomplete recovery.
rationale: Cram-down is the power of the court to approve a rehabilitation plan despite creditor objections, provided the plan is fair and equitable.
canonicalConcept: Cram-down power of rehabilitation court

prompt: It is a liquidation of insolvent businessman which is initiated by the debtor himself.
rationale: Voluntary liquidation is initiated by the debtor himself, as opposed to involuntary liquidation initiated by creditors.
canonicalConcept: Voluntary vs involuntary liquidation

prompt: It refers to the government agency entrusted to implement the national competition policy and the objectives and purposes of Philippine Competition Act.
rationale: The Philippine Competition Commission (PCC) is the independent quasi-judicial body created under RA 10667 to enforce the Philippine Competition Act.
canonicalConcept: Philippine Competition Commission as implementing agency of PCA

prompt: What type of merger or acquisition agreements is prohibited by Philippine Competition Act?

choices.text: Merger or acquisition agreements that substantially prevent, restrict or lessen competition in the relevant market or in the market for goods or services.

rationale: The PCA prohibits mergers or acquisitions that substantially prevent, restrict, or lessen competition (SPRCL) in the relevant market.
canonicalConcept: Prohibited mergers and acquisitions under PCA: SPRCL standard

prompt: It refers to a method of procurement which is open to participation by any interested party and which consists of the following processes: advertisement, pre-bid conference, eligibility screening of bids, evaluations of bids, post-qualification, and award of contract.
rationale: Competitive bidding (public bidding) is the default method of procurement under RA 9184.
canonicalConcept: Competitive bidding as default procurement method under RA 9184

prompt: Who has the responsibility to prepare the bidding documents?
rationale: Under RA 9184, the procuring entity is responsible for preparing the bidding documents.
canonicalConcept: Responsibility for preparation of bidding documents under RA 9184

prompt: He refers to a partner who contributed service or industry.
rationale: An industrial partner contributes service or industry (labor/skills). A capitalist partner contributes money or property.
canonicalConcept: Types of partners: industrial partner vs capitalist partner

prompt: Which of the following may not be contributed by a pure limited partner?
rationale: A limited partner cannot contribute pure services or industry; only capital (money or property) may be contributed.
canonicalConcept: Limited partner contributions: service cannot be contributed by pure limited partner

prompt: Which of the following statements concerning the obligations and rights of a partner is incorrect?

choices.text: Every partner shall at any reasonable hour have access to and may inspect and copy any of the partnership books.

Every partner shall render on demand true and full information of all things affecting the partnership to any partner or the legal representative of any deceased partner or of any partner under legal disability.

Every partner must account to the partnership for any benefit, and hold as trustee for it any profits derived by him without the consent of the other partners from any transaction connected with the formation, conduct, or liquidation of the partnership or from any use by him of its property.
Every capitalist partner can engage for their own account in any operation which is of the same kind of business in which the partnership is engaged.

rationale: A capitalist partner cannot engage in the same kind of business as the partnership without the consent of the other partners.
canonicalConcept: Partner obligations: duty of loyalty and prohibition against competing business

prompt: It is a principle which means that a partner has a right to choose those whom he wants to be associated with the partnership.
rationale: Delectus personae is the principle that partnership is based on mutual trust and confidence, giving each partner the right to choose his associates.
canonicalConcept: Delectus personae in partnerships

prompt: Which of the following statements pertains to partnership by estoppel?

choices.text: It is a partnership where all the partners are liable to the extent of their separate property after the partnership assets have been exhausted.

It is a partnership where there is at least one general partner who is liable up to the extent of his separate assets and at least one limited partner who is liable up to the extent of his investment in the partnership.
It is a partnership which actually exists among the partners as well as to third persons.
It is a partnership which in reality is not a partnership but is considered as one with respect to those who, by reason of their conduct or admission, are precluded from denying its existence.

rationale: Partnership by estoppel arises when persons who are not actually partners hold themselves out as partners, and third persons rely on such representation.
canonicalConcept: Partnership by estoppel: definition and legal effect

prompt: The following are the rights of a partner in a partnership, except

choices.text: To associate another person with him in his share.
To admit another person into the partnership without the consent of all the partners.
To have access to and inspect and copy the partnership books at reasonable hours.
To have formal account of partnership affairs.

rationale: A partner cannot admit another person into the partnership without the consent of all the other partners (delectus personae).
canonicalConcept: Rights of partners: unanimous consent required for admission of new partners

prompt: Who among the following may not be insured?
rationale: A public enemy (alien enemy in time of war) cannot be insured because they have no insurable interest recognized by the insurer.
canonicalConcept: Insurable interest: public enemy cannot be insured

prompt: It refers to a neglect to communicate that which a party knows and ought to communicate.
rationale: Concealment in insurance is the neglect to communicate what a party knows and ought to communicate.
canonicalConcept: Concealment in insurance contracts

prompt: How many years is the incontestability clause of life insurance in case of death of the insured by reason of fraudulent concealment or misrepresentation by the insured or his agent whereby the insurance company can no longer prove that the policy is void ab initio or is rescindible?

choices.text: One (1) year from the date of its issue or of its last reinstatement.
Two (2) years from the date of its issue or of its last reinstatement.
Three (3) years from the date of its issue or of its last reinstatement.
Four (4) years from the date of its issue or of its last reinstatement.

rationale: Under the Insurance Code, a life insurance policy becomes incontestable after two (2) years from the date of issue or last reinstatement.
canonicalConcept: Incontestability clause in life insurance: two-year period

prompt: It is an artificial being created by operation of law, having the right of succession and the powers, attributes and properties expressly authorized by law or incident to its existence.
rationale: This is the classic definition of a corporation under Section 2 of the Revised Corporation Code.
canonicalConcept: Definition of a corporation under Section 2 RCC

prompt: A corporation with a single stockholder.
rationale: A One Person Corporation (OPC) is a corporation with a single stockholder, expressly recognized under RA 11232.
canonicalConcept: One Person Corporation under RA 11232

prompt: The primary test being used to determine the nationality of a corporation
rationale: The Control Test is the primary test for determining corporate nationality.
canonicalConcept: Control Test as primary test for corporate nationality

prompt: The method by which the percentage of Filipino equity in a corporation engaged in nationalized and/or partly nationalized areas of activities is accurately computed, in cases where corporate shareholders with foreign shareholdings are present, by attributing the nationality of the second or even subsequent tier of ownership to determine the nationality of the corporation shareholders.
rationale: The Grandfather Rule looks beyond the first tier of ownership to determine actual nationality of shareholders in nationalized industries.
canonicalConcept: Grandfather Rule for determining nationality in nationalized industries

prompt: Corporate existence and juridical personality commences from:

choices.text: Submission of requirements to the SEC.
Date of Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation of SEC.
Signing of the Articles of Incorporation.

rationale: Under Section 19 RCC, corporate existence commences from the date of issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation by the SEC.
canonicalConcept: Commencement of corporate existence: issuance of certificate of incorporation

prompt: An equitable remedy developed to address situations where the separate corporate personality of a corporation is abused or used for wrongful purposes.

choices.text: Doctrine of Piercing the Corporate Veil.

rationale: Piercing the corporate veil is an equitable remedy where the court disregards separate corporate personality and holds shareholders personally liable.
canonicalConcept: Doctrine of piercing the corporate veil as equitable remedy

prompt: I. Death of a stockholder dissolves a corporation. II. Educational institutions can be a stock corporation. III. Insurance companies cannot be incorporated as a close corporation.

choices.text: I is true, II is false and III is true.
I is false, II is true and III is true.

rationale: Death of a stockholder does not dissolve a corporation (right of succession). Educational institutions can be stock corporations. Insurance companies cannot be close corporations.
canonicalConcept: Characteristics of corporations: death of stockholder does not dissolve; educational stock corporations; insurance companies cannot be close corporations

prompt: A non-stock corporation is composed of
rationale: Non-stock corporations have members, not stockholders.
canonicalConcept: Non-stock corporations composed of members not stockholders

prompt: Refer to the diagram: ABC Corporation (Public utility corporation) is 60% owned by XYZ Corporation and 40% by Foreigners. XYZ Corporation is 60% Filipino and 40% Foreigners. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.text: ABC Corporation cannot be owned by foreigners.
ABC Corporation is a foreign corporation.
ABC Corporation is a domestic corporation.
XYZ Corporation is a foreign corporation.

rationale: ABC is incorporated in the Philippines (domestic). Under the Grandfather Rule, XYZ's 60% stake in ABC is attributed 60% Filipino and 40% foreign based on XYZ's stockholders. Thus ABC meets the 60% Filipino requirement for public utilities.
canonicalConcept: Grandfather Rule application: public utility corporation nationality computation

prompt: Based on the diagram, which of the following statements is not true?

choices.text: XYZ Corporation is a domestic corporation.
Since XYZ Corporation is 40% foreign owned, ABC Corporation is no longer a Filipino corporation.
Foreigners only own 40% of ABC Corporation.

rationale: The statement is false because under the Grandfather Rule, we attribute the nationality of XYZ's stockholders to its stake in ABC. XYZ is 60% Filipino, so its 60% stake in ABC is considered 36% Filipino + 24% foreign. Combined with direct 40% foreign ownership, ABC still meets requirements.
canonicalConcept: Grandfather Rule: effect of foreign ownership in parent company on subsidiary nationality

prompt: The test used in this diagram is called
rationale: The Control Test looks at the nationality of controlling stockholders. Since XYZ is 60% Filipino, it is Filipino-controlled, and thus ABC is 60% Filipino-owned.
canonicalConcept: Control Test vs Grandfather Rule in corporate nationality determination

prompt: In which of the following instances may the Court pierce the veil of corporate fiction?

choices.text: The nationality of the corporation is unknown.
The corporation is owned by foreigners.
The corporation is being used as an alter ego of another corporation.
The corporation is owned by Filipinos.

rationale: The court may pierce the corporate veil when the corporation is merely an alter ego of another corporation or its stockholders.
canonicalConcept: Grounds for piercing the corporate veil: alter ego doctrine

prompt: A basic contract document, defining the charter of the corporation, and serves as the basis by which to judge whether it exists for legal purposes.
rationale: The Articles of Incorporation is the charter document that defines the corporation's essential details.
canonicalConcept: Articles of Incorporation as corporate charter

prompt: It is a basic class of stock ordinarily and usually issued without extraordinary rights or privileges and entitles the shareholder to a pro rata division of profits.
rationale: Common or ordinary shares are the basic class of stock with no special privileges other than pro rata division of profits and assets.
canonicalConcept: Common/ordinary shares: definition and characteristics

prompt: The Articles of Incorporation must contain the following except:
rationale: The AOI must contain corporate name, purpose, principal office, term, incorporators, capital stock, etc. The name of the promoter is not required.
canonicalConcept: Contents of Articles of Incorporation under Section 14 RCC

prompt: Under the Revised Corporation Code, if the Articles of Incorporation does not state the corporate term, corporate term will be:
rationale: Under Section 11 RCC, if no term is stated, the corporation shall have perpetual existence.
canonicalConcept: Perpetual existence under Section 11 RCC when no term is stated

prompt: Under this doctrine, each share shall be equal in all respects to every other share, except as otherwise provided in the Articles of Incorporation and stated in the certificate of stock.

choices.text: Doctrine of Piercing the Corporate Veil.
Doctrine of Equality in a Corporation.

rationale: The Doctrine of Equality of Shares (Section 6, RCC) provides that each share is equal to every other share unless the AOI provides otherwise.
canonicalConcept: Doctrine of Equality of Shares under Section 6 RCC

prompt: Are the types of contracts entered into in behalf of a corporation which is in the process of organization and incorporation, and such fact is acknowledged as an essential ingredient in the process of perfection.
rationale: Pre-incorporation contracts are entered into by promoters on behalf of a corporation still being formed. They are not binding unless ratified after incorporation.
canonicalConcept: Pre-incorporation contracts: definition and binding effect

prompt: Remo, James, and Arthur incorporated ABC College, an educational corporation for profit and had it listed in the Philippine Stock Exchange to sell its shares. Can ABC College be incorporated as a stock corporation?

choices.text: No, because education should not be for profit.
Yes, because an educational corporation can be a stock corporation.
Yes, because it is a stock corporation.
No, because educational corporations must be non-stock corporations.

rationale: Under RCC, educational corporations may be organized as stock corporations, except those established by religious groups or missions.
canonicalConcept: Educational corporations may be stock corporations under RCC

prompt: Ana and Ruby bought shares of ABC Mall as stockholders. Ana and Ruby went to ABC Mall, instead of buying items at the mall, they took several shoes and makeup items claiming that as stockholders they own the mall and thus, all items inside it. Is Ana and Ruby's statement correct?

choices.text: Yes, because they are stockholders of ABC Mall.
No, because they should buy it.
No, because the corporate property is owned by the corporation as a juridical person, and the stockholders have no claim on corporate property as owners.

rationale: Stockholders are not owners of corporate property. The corporation has separate juridical personality and owns its assets.
canonicalConcept: Separate juridical personality: stockholders do not own corporate property

prompt: A suit brought by a stockholder for and on behalf of the corporation for its protection from the wrongful acts committed by the directors/trustees of the corporation, when the stockholder finds that he has no redress because the directors/trustees are the ones vested by law to decide whether or not to sue.
rationale: A derivative suit is filed by a stockholder on behalf of the corporation to redress wrongs committed against it when the corporation refuses to sue.
canonicalConcept: Derivative suit: definition and requirements

prompt: The right to withdraw from the corporation and demand payment of the fair value of the shares after dissenting from certain corporate acts involving fundamental changes in corporate structure.
rationale: Appraisal right is the right of a dissenting stockholder to demand payment of fair value of his shares when he votes against fundamental corporate changes.
canonicalConcept: Appraisal right of dissenting stockholders

prompt: Ana is a stockholder of ABS-GMA Network. During the stockholder's meeting, the Board of Directors voted in favor of using the corporate funds to buy shares of Microsoft at the New York Stock Exchange. Ana disagreed with the proposal but instead of voting No, she opted to abstain because of fear that the other stockholders might be offended. Can Ana exercise her appraisal right?

choices.text: No, because there is no appraisal right for corporate decisions involving investing corporate funds to another corporation.
No, because stockholder must have voted against the corporate action in order to exercise his/her appraisal right.
Yes, because she is a prejudiced stockholder.
No, she should file an injunction before the Regional Trial Court to stop the corporate action.

rationale: To exercise appraisal right, the stockholder must have voted against the proposed corporate action. Abstention does not qualify.
canonicalConcept: Appraisal right requirement: must vote against the corporate action

prompt: Questions of policy or management are left solely to the honest decision of officers and directors of a corporation and the courts are without authority to substitute their judgment for the judgment of the board of directors is called
rationale: The Business Judgment Rule protects directors and officers from liability for honest mistakes or errors in judgment made in good faith.
canonicalConcept: Business Judgment Rule: protection for honest decisions of directors

prompt: Under this doctrine, unless otherwise provided in this Code, the board of directors or trustees shall exercise the corporate powers, conduct all business, and control all properties of the corporation.

choices.text: Doctrine of Piercing the Corporate Veil.

rationale: The Doctrine of Centralized Management vests all corporate powers in the board of directors/trustees.
canonicalConcept: Doctrine of Centralized Management: board exercises corporate powers

prompt: It is defined as a corporation that absorbs the other and remains in existence while the others are dissolved.
rationale: In a merger, one corporation (surviving) absorbs another (constituent) and remains in existence while the absorbed corporation is dissolved.
canonicalConcept: Merger vs consolidation: surviving corporation absorbs constituent

prompt: Under Revised Corporation Code, which private corporation is prohibited from giving donations in aid of any political party or candidate or for purposes of partisan political activity?
rationale: Under Section 36 RCC, foreign corporations are prohibited from making donations for partisan political activities.
canonicalConcept: Foreign corporation prohibition on partisan political donations

prompt: What is the required vote for incurring, creating or increasing bond indebtedness?

choices.text: Approval by at least majority vote of the board of directors/trustees and ratification by stockholders representing at least 2/3 of the outstanding capital stock or at least 2/3 of members.
Approval by stockholders representing at least 2/3 of the outstanding capital stock or members.
Approval by at least majority vote of the board of directors/trustees and ratification by stockholders representing at least majority of the outstanding capital stock or members.
Approval by at least majority vote of the board of directors/trustees.

rationale: Under Section 38 RCC, bond indebtedness requires majority board approval and ratification by stockholders representing at least 2/3 of outstanding capital stock.
canonicalConcept: Vote requirement for bond indebtedness under Section 38 RCC

prompt: When no-par value common shares of stocks are issued, what is the minimum issue price?
rationale: Under RCC, no-par value shares cannot be issued for less than P5.00 per share.
canonicalConcept: Minimum issue price of no-par value shares: P5.00

prompt: In which meeting is proxy allowed?
rationale: Proxy is allowed in stockholders' or members' meetings but not in board meetings due to the personal nature of directors' duties.
canonicalConcept: Proxy voting allowed in stockholders meetings but not board meetings

prompt: The maximum deposit insurance coverage under the PDIC Law.
rationale: The maximum deposit insurance coverage is currently P500,000 under RA 9576. However, review materials may cite updated amounts. The answer key indicates D.
canonicalConcept: PDIC maximum deposit insurance coverage

prompt: The liability of PDIC on the determination of insured deposit due to the depositors of a closed bank commences on

choices.text: The notice of closure of bank issued by the BSP.
Actual takeover of the closed bank.
Upon service of summons to the closed bank.

rationale: PDIC liability commences from actual takeover of the closed bank.
canonicalConcept: PDIC liability commencement: actual takeover of closed bank

prompt: Vice President Y is on impeachment trial over alleged use of confidential funds for her personal benefit. Can the Senate of the Philippines inquire the deposits of Vice President Y in various banks?

choices.text: Yes, because this is a case of impeachment.
No, because Vice President Y is protected under the Bank Secrecy Law.
No, because Vice President Y has not yet issued a written permission.
Yes, because she used confidential funds.

rationale: Under RA 1405, bank deposits may be inquired into in cases of impeachment.
canonicalConcept: Bank secrecy exception: impeachment cases under RA 1405

prompt: Billionaire X died of COVID-19 leaving his assets and business empire worth Php 100 billion to his family. Can the Commissioner of Internal Revenue inquire into his bank accounts?

choices.text: Yes, because he died of COVID-19.
No, because it is a violation of the Bank Secrecy Law.
Yes, in order to determine the value of his estate for tax purposes.
No, because X did not leave a written authority to do so.

rationale: Under Section 6(F) NIRC and RA 1405, the BIR Commissioner may inquire into bank deposits of a decedent to determine gross estate for estate tax purposes.
canonicalConcept: Bank secrecy exception: BIR inquiry for estate tax determination

prompt: R.A. Act No. 3765, otherwise known as the Truth in Lending Act, applies to:
rationale: The Truth in Lending Act applies to all credit transactions. However, the answer key indicates D. Note: This may be an error in the answer key; the law generally covers all creditors including pawnshops and money lenders.
canonicalConcept: Truth in Lending Act coverage and scope

prompt: Under Truth in Lending Act, what is the prescriptive period available to debtor to recover civil penalty from the creditor who fails to make proper disclosure about the true cost of financing of a credit transaction?

choices.text: Within one (1) year from the date of the occurrence of the violation.
Within two (2) years from the date of the occurrence of the violation.
Within three (3) years from the date of the occurrence of the violation.
Within four (4) years from the date of the occurrence of the violation.

rationale: Under RA 3765, the prescriptive period to recover civil penalty is one (1) year from the date of the violation.
canonicalConcept: Truth in Lending Act prescriptive period: one year

prompt: Jose is a client of BBB Bank. One day, he went to the bank, and said he wanted to open an account in BBB Bank for Php 10 million but he asked that it be put under his fictitious name 'Coco Dantes' because he wants to prevent his wife, Mae from finding out the money subject of this deposit. Can BBB Bank open an account for Jose under the name 'Coco Dantes'?

choices.text: Yes, because BBB Bank knows it is Jose.
Yes, because he is a client and it's allowed under the Anti-Money Laundering Act.
No, because Mae's consent is needed.
No, because the Anti-Money Laundering Act prohibits such act.

rationale: Under AMLA, opening an account under a fictitious name is prohibited. Covered persons must require proof of identity.
canonicalConcept: AMLA prohibition on fictitious name accounts

prompt: Who among the following is not part of Anti-Money Laundering Council?

choices.text: BSP Governor as chairperson of AMLC.
Insurance Commissioner as member of AMLC.
SEC Chairperson as member of AMLC.
BIR Commissioner as member of AMLC.

rationale: The AMLC is composed of the BSP Governor (Chair), Insurance Commissioner, and SEC Chairperson. The BIR Commissioner is not a member.
canonicalConcept: AMLC composition: BSP Governor, Insurance Commissioner, SEC Chairperson

prompt: What is the minimum retention period of all records of customer identification and transaction documents of their customers by a covered person under Anti-Money Laundering Law?

choices.text: At least 1 year from the date of transaction or from date of closure of the account.
At least 3 years from the date of transaction or from date of closure of the account.
At least 5 years from the date of transaction or from date of closure of the account.
At least 10 years from the date of transaction or from date of closure of the account.

rationale: Under AMLA, covered persons must retain records for at least five (5) years from the date of transaction or closure of account.
canonicalConcept: AMLA record retention period: five years

prompt: This principle means that No administrative, criminal or civil proceedings shall lie against any person for having made a covered transaction report in the regular performance of his duties and in good faith, whether or not such reporting results in any criminal prosecution under the AMLA or any other Philippine law.
rationale: The safe harbor provision protects covered persons from liability for reporting suspicious transactions in good faith.
canonicalConcept: AMLA safe harbor provision for good faith reporting

prompt: Which of the following is not a suspicious transaction and therefore shall not be reported to Anti-Money Laundering Council?

choices.text: Transaction that has no underlying legal or trade obligation, purpose or economic justification.
Transaction in which the client is properly identified.
Transaction in which the amount involved is not commensurate with the business or financial capacity of the client.
Transaction that deviates from the profile of the client.

rationale: A transaction where the client is properly identified is not inherently suspicious. Suspicious transactions include those with no legal justification, amounts not commensurate with capacity, or deviations from client profile.
canonicalConcept: Suspicious transaction indicators under AMLA

prompt: Which court has jurisdiction to issue an order authorizing the AMLC to inquire or examine any particular deposit or investment account including related accounts with a banking institution or non-bank financial institution based on the ex parte application by AMLC in cases of violation of AMLA?
rationale: Under AMLA, the Court of Appeals has jurisdiction to issue freeze orders and authorize examination of bank accounts upon ex parte application by AMLC.
canonicalConcept: AMLA court jurisdiction: Court of Appeals for freeze orders

prompt: Which of the following are copyrightable works: I. The decisions of the Supreme Court written by Chief Justice Gesmundo. II. The split-up of Kathryn Bernardo and Daniel Padilla. III. A tell-all book written by Aljur Abrenica detailing all his relationships. IV. Letters written by Dingdong Dantes to Marian Rivera. V. The song 'Golden'.
rationale: Court decisions and news of public interest are not copyrightable. Original literary works (books, letters) and musical works (songs) are copyrightable.
canonicalConcept: Copyrightable works: original literary and musical works vs public domain

prompt: The controlling test to determine whether the marks are confusingly similar?
rationale: The Dominancy Test is used to determine confusing similarity of trademarks by focusing on the dominant features of the mark.
canonicalConcept: Dominancy Test for trademark confusing similarity

prompt: It is the disclosure or transfer to a third party of personal data under the custody of a personal information controller or personal information processor.
rationale: Data sharing is the disclosure or transfer to a third party of personal data under the custody of a personal information controller or processor.
canonicalConcept: Data sharing definition under RA 10173

prompt: In entering into any contract with a private service provider that may involve accessing or requiring sensitive personal information, when shall the government agency require such service provider and its employees to register their personal data processing system with the National Privacy Commission?

choices.text: When the processing of sensitive personal information involves one hundred (100) or more individuals.
When the processing of sensitive personal information involves ten thousands (10,000) or more individuals.
When the processing of sensitive personal information involves five hundred (500) or more individuals.
When the processing of sensitive personal information involves one thousand (1,000) or more individuals.

rationale: Under the Data Privacy Act, registration is required when processing sensitive personal information of at least 1,000 individuals.
canonicalConcept: NPC registration threshold: 1,000 individuals for sensitive personal data

prompt: Which of the following is not a sensitive personal information?

choices.text: Information about an individual's race, ethnic origin, marital status, age, color, and religious, philosophical or political affiliations.

Information about an individual's health, education, genetic or sexual life of a person, or to any proceeding for any offense committed or alleged to have been committed by such individual, the disposal of such proceedings, or the sentence of any court in such proceedings.

Information issued by government agencies peculiar to an individual which includes, but is not limited to, social security numbers, previous or current health records, licenses or its denials, suspension or revocation, and tax returns.
Information about an individual's name, address, and contact details used for ordinary business transactions.

rationale: Name, address, and contact details are personal information, not sensitive personal information. Sensitive personal information includes race, health, education, sexual life, offenses, and government-issued identifiers.
canonicalConcept: Sensitive personal information vs personal information under RA 10173

prompt: Which of the following is within the sphere of application of E-Commerce Act?
rationale: The E-Commerce Act (RA 8792) applies to both commercial and non-commercial activities involving electronic data messages and electronic documents.
canonicalConcept: E-Commerce Act scope: commercial and non-commercial activities

prompt: He refers to a person by whom, or on whose behalf, the electronic document purports to have been created, generated and/or sent.
rationale: The originator is the person by whom or on whose behalf the electronic document is created, generated, or sent.
canonicalConcept: Originator definition under E-Commerce Act

prompt: It refers to any regulation, rule, or administrative procedure or system that is ineffective or detrimental in achieving its intended objectives and, as a result, produces slow, suboptimal, and undesirable social outcomes.
rationale: Red tape refers to excessive regulation, rigid conformity to formal rules, and bureaucratic delay that hinders efficient government service.
canonicalConcept: Red tape definition under Ease of Doing Business Act

prompt: It refers to the process or transaction between applicants or requesting parties and government offices or agencies involving applications for any privilege, right, reward, license, clearance, permit or authorization, concession, or for any modification, renewal or extension of the enumerated applications or requests which are acted upon in the ordinary course of business of the agency or office.
rationale: Government service refers to transactions between applicants and government offices involving applications for privileges, licenses, permits, and similar authorizations.
canonicalConcept: Government service definition under Ease of Doing Business Act

prompt: It refers to the minimum amount of remuneration that an employer is required to pay wage earners for the work performed during a given period, which cannot be reduced by collective agreement or an individual contract. It is the lowest wage rate fixed by law that an employer can pay his employees.
rationale: Minimum wage is the lowest wage rate fixed by law that an employer can pay his employees, which cannot be reduced by collective agreement or individual contract.
canonicalConcept: Minimum wage definition under Labor Code

prompt: What is the rate of overtime pay premium for overtime work on holiday or rest day?

choices.text: 25% of the holiday or rest day rate.
30% of the holiday or rest day rate.
35% of the holiday or rest day rate.
40% of the holiday or rest day rate.

rationale: Under the Labor Code, overtime work on a holiday or rest day is paid with an additional 30% of the holiday/rest day rate.
canonicalConcept: Overtime premium on holiday or rest day: 30%

prompt: What is the nature of funds of Social Security System?

choices.text: The funds contributed to the SSS are confidential funds.
The funds contributed to the SSS are private funds belonging to the members are merely held in trust by the government.
The funds contributed to the SSS are governmental funds.
The funds contributed to the SSS are state funds.

rationale: SSS funds are private funds belonging to the members, held in trust by the government. They are not government or state funds.
canonicalConcept: SSS funds nature: private funds held in trust

prompt: What is the amount of sickness benefit under SSS Law?

choices.text: The amount of the member's daily sickness benefit allowance is equivalent to 80% of his/her average daily salary credit.
The amount of the member's daily sickness benefit allowance is equivalent to 70% of his/her average daily salary credit.
The amount of the member's daily sickness benefit allowance is equivalent to 75% of his/her average daily salary credit.
The amount of the member's daily sickness benefit allowance is equivalent to 90% of his/her average daily salary credit.

rationale: Under the SSS Law, the daily sickness benefit allowance is equivalent to 90% of the member's average daily salary credit.
canonicalConcept: SSS sickness benefit: 90% of average daily salary credit
